title: Lean Manufacturing
tagline: Eliminate waste, streamline shopfloor operations, and instill continuous improvement discipline.
problem: Manufacturing plants suffer from invisible shopfloor waste, excessive motion, overproduction, and defects that inflate operating costs and degrade productivity.
approach: Step 1: Conduct shopfloor diagnostic and 7 Waste (Muda) audit across value streams.
Step 2: Implement 5S workplace organization and visual controls.
Step 3: Map current state Value Streams and design future state target flows.
Step 4: Train frontline operators and supervisors in Kaizen and structured problem-solving.
Step 5: Establish Daily Management Systems (DMS) and standard work audits.
typicalOutcomes: 25-40% reduction in non-value-adding activity time
30% improvement in shopfloor space utilization
20% decrease in operational defects and rework

title: Operational Excellence
tagline: Align management systems, culture, and processes for sustainable peak manufacturing performance.
problem: Fragmented improvement initiatives often fail to sustain, resulting in inconsistent performance, lack of accountability, and disconnected KPIs across management tiers.
approach: Step 1: Perform comprehensive operational health check and leadership alignment.
Step 2: Establish cascading visual KPI management systems from COO to shopfloor.
Step 3: Define standardized management operating cadences and daily standups.
Step 4: Deploy capability-building programs for plant managers and shift supervisors.
Step 5: Implement governance models and sustaining audit mechanisms.
typicalOutcomes: 15-30% plant-wide productivity enhancement
Sustainable execution culture with high frontline accountability
95%+ adherence to operational target metrics

title: Industrial Engineering
tagline: Scientific time-and-motion analysis to optimize work content, ergonomics, and productivity.
problem: Unmeasured work methods and subjective standard times lead to inaccurate labor costing, low worker productivity, and inefficient workstation design.
approach: Step 1: Execute detailed MOST (Maynard Operation Sequence Technique) or stop-watch time studies.
Step 2: Analyze operator movements, ergonomics, and non-value-adding motion.
Step 3: Redesign workstations and tool positioning for optimal human-machine synergy.
Step 4: Establish standardized work instructions and cycle time baselines.
Step 5: Roll out multi-skilling matrix and operator skill verification.
typicalOutcomes: 20-35% improvement in labor productivity
Accurate standard time baselines for precise scheduling
Ergonomics improvement reducing fatigue and injuries

title: Factory Layout Optimisation
tagline: Design lean, continuous-flow plant layouts that eliminate travel waste and maximize space.
problem: Haphazard historical expansion creates crisscrossing material flows, long travel distances, congested aisles, and wasted floor space.
approach: Step 1: Map existing material travel routes using spaghetti diagrams and quantitative flow matrices.
Step 2: Analyze machine footprint, utility requirements, and safety clearances.
Step 3: Design cellular and unidirectional flow layouts prioritizing product families.
Step 4: Simulate material handling logistics and buffer allocations.
Step 5: Execute phased machine relocation with minimal production downtime.
typicalOutcomes: 35% reduction in material handling and operator movement distance
25% floor space freed up for future expansion
Compressed overall manufacturing lead times

title: Production Planning
tagline: Synchronize demand with shopfloor scheduling to eliminate inventory build-up and missed shipments.
problem: Uncoordinated scheduling, frequent plan changes, and push production lead to excessive WIP, stockouts of critical parts, and late customer deliveries.
approach: Step 1: Analyze demand variability and establish product categorization (ABC/XYZ analysis).
Step 2: Implement Drum-Buffer-Rope or Kanban demand-pull scheduling mechanisms.
Step 3: Design visual production boards and daily scheduling update routines.
Step 4: Align raw material procurement with finite shopfloor capacity schedules.
Step 5: Train planning teams on dynamic leveling (Heijunka) techniques.
typicalOutcomes: 30% reduction in Work-In-Progress (WIP) inventory
98%+ On-Time In-Full (OTIF) delivery compliance
Elimination of rush orders and schedule chaos

title: Capacity Improvement
tagline: Unlock hidden plant capacity and expand output without expensive machinery Capex.
problem: Manufacturers believe their plant is running at max capacity and plan major capital expenditure, unaware that 20-35% hidden capacity is locked in bottlenecks and micro-stoppages.
approach: Step 1: Perform plant-wide capacity modeling to pinpoint physical constraint stations.
Step 2: Sub-optimize non-bottlenecks to ensure continuous feeding of constraint equipment.
Step 3: Eliminate constraint downtime using targeted TPM and quick setup methods.
Step 4: Balance upstream and downstream process speeds with constraint pace.
Step 5: Establish constraint buffer management and real-time output monitoring.
typicalOutcomes: 20-35% output capacity expansion on existing equipment
Capex deferral or complete avoidance
Reduced unit production cost

title: OEE Improvement
tagline: Maximize equipment availability, performance rate, and quality output on critical assets.
problem: Low equipment availability due to breakdowns, minor stoppages, speed losses, and quality rejects keeps OEE trapped between 40-60%.
approach: Step 1: Install standardized OEE data capture and loss categorization framework.
Step 2: Conduct 6 Big Losses analysis to pinpoint major downtime contributors.
Step 3: Deploy Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Planned Maintenance (PM) pillars.
Step 4: Execute SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) setup time reduction projects.
Step 5: Institutionalize Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and 5-Why problem solving.
typicalOutcomes: 18% OEE Improvement across key asset groups
72% Changeover Reduction (setup time)
Significant decrease in unpredicted equipment breakdowns

title: Digitalization & Automation
tagline: Deploy smart digital dashboards, IoT tracking, and low-cost automation to digitize shopfloor operations.
problem: Paper-based shopfloor logs, manual data entry delays, and lack of real-time visibility into machine downtime, scrap, and line output.
approach: Step 1: Install digital shopfloor tracking & real-time visual OEE dashboards.
Step 2: Deploy Low Cost Automation (LCIA) and Poka-Yoke error-proofing sensors.
Step 3: Automate daily production reporting and downtime categorization.
Step 4: Connect critical machines for live cycle time and breakdown monitoring.
Step 5: Train supervisors on real-time digital management operating cadences.
typicalOutcomes: Real-time shopfloor visibility & automated downtime tracking
Zero-defect quality assurance through automated Poka-Yoke sensors
Elimination of manual paper log sheets and reporting lag

title: Material Flow
tagline: Streamline raw material, WIP, and finished goods movement from dock to dispatch.
problem: Chaotic material handling, double-handling of parts, misplaced inventory, and delayed line feeding disrupt production schedules and inflate logistics costs.
approach: Step 1: Analyze material movement paths, lot sizes, and handling equipment utilization.
Step 2: Design Mizusumashi (water-spider) timed material supply routes to workstations.
Step 3: Establish supermarket storage zones with min-max inventory controls.
Step 4: Implement Kanban signaling and FIFO (First-In, First-Out) material flow.
Step 5: Standardize container sizes, kit packaging, and visual material status.
typicalOutcomes: 30% Lead Time Reduction
Elimination of shopfloor line starvation due to part shortages
50% reduction in material double-handling

title: Cost Reduction
tagline: Identify and eliminate structural manufacturing costs without compromising product quality.
problem: Rising raw material prices, labor costs, and high scrap rates squeeze profit margins, making cost reduction a strategic necessity for manufacturing plants.
approach: Step 1: Conduct cost-driver analysis across conversion, labor, energy, and scrap categories.
Step 2: Map energy consumption baselines and identify power waste in utilities.
Step 3: Execute yield optimization projects to minimize scrap and raw material loss.
Step 4: Optimize manpower deployment and reduce overtime reliance.
Step 5: Establish plant cost-tracking dashboards and continuous savings pipeline.
typicalOutcomes: 10-20% reduction in unit conversion cost
Significant scrap and material yield improvement
Direct margin expansion for manufacturing operations
